correctness.rationale: The proof uses a sharp fixed-increment variance inequality from absolute continuity and uniform pushforward domination, attained by centered Lipschitz ramps. Independent cells reduce the risk to a separable cubic allocation. Pairwise exact exchange proves an equal-positive-entry maximizer and therefore a finite integer formula; differentiation gives all boundaries and regimes. The standalone verifier passed 4,816 exact-rational assertions and an independently executed continuous numerical optimization stress test found no counterexample. Finite checks corroborate, but do not replace, the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The closest complete primary source, Basak–Bect–Vazquez 2022 Theorem 4.1, proves the unbounded-slope monotone result with discontinuous step extremizers. Neither its bound nor the standard Lipschitz variance bound specifies the exact intermediate finite-slope constant or sparse allocation. Kunsch 2023 and Pettersson–Krumscheid 2021 address different function classes, objectives or sample-allocation designs. Relevant prior maximal-variance inequalities could cover components; incomplete access is disclosed rather than treated as proof of noncoverage.

value.rationale: The theorem determines a natural sharp worst-case risk for the intersection of bounded monotone and Lipschitz classes, at every n and L. It reveals exact centered-ramp extremizers, a quantized support-size optimization and two smoothness transitions, sharpening both the general monotone step bound and simple Lipschitz variance estimates. The full finite-n classification is useful as a test case for shape-constrained randomized integration and needs no downstream theorem.
